uxReferencePatterns.label: Material navigation and information architecture
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Apple HIG navigation and content organization
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Make navigation predictable, content-centered, and appropriate for the user’s current task.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Material Design cards and lists
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Material detail surface composition
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Build a domain detail page with primary content, metadata, status, and actions instead of a generic task card.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Review-and-confirm payment flow
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Use a review/confirmation step with amount, payer context, recipient, fees or entitlement, receipt, and audit trail.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Multi-step payment/progress flow
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Use explicit progress states for checkout, review, confirmation, receipt, and entitlement/status.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Form validation and review pattern
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Copy a form flow with field labels, helper text, validation errors, review state, submit action, status, and protected-data treatment.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Inbox and message thread pattern
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Copy an inbox/thread structure: sender, timestamp, message preview/body, reply field, invite/block state, and read/received state.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Screenshot-first critique method
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Critique must quote visible UI/text, name the persona and task, compare against the chosen reference pattern, and state the exact fix.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Material navigation and information architecture
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Apple HIG navigation and content organization
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Make navigation predictable, content-centered, and appropriate for the user’s current task.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Material Design cards and lists
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Material detail surface composition
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Build a domain detail page with primary content, metadata, status, and actions instead of a generic task card.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Review-and-confirm payment flow
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Use a review/confirmation step with amount, payer context, recipient, fees or entitlement, receipt, and audit trail.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Multi-step payment/progress flow
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Use explicit progress states for checkout, review, confirmation, receipt, and entitlement/status.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Form validation and review pattern
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Copy a form flow with field labels, helper text, validation errors, review state, submit action, status, and protected-data treatment.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Inbox and message thread pattern
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Copy an inbox/thread structure: sender, timestamp, message preview/body, reply field, invite/block state, and read/received state.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Material navigation and information architecture
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Apple HIG navigation and content organization
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Make navigation predictable, content-centered, and appropriate for the user’s current task.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Material Design cards and lists
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Material detail surface composition
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Build a domain detail page with primary content, metadata, status, and actions instead of a generic task card.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Review-and-confirm payment flow
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Use a review/confirmation step with amount, payer context, recipient, fees or entitlement, receipt, and audit trail.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Multi-step payment/progress flow
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Use explicit progress states for checkout, review, confirmation, receipt, and entitlement/status.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Form validation and review pattern
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Copy a form flow with field labels, helper text, validation errors, review state, submit action, status, and protected-data treatment.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Inbox and message thread pattern
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Copy an inbox/thread structure: sender, timestamp, message preview/body, reply field, invite/block state, and read/received state.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Screenshot-first critique method
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Critique must quote visible UI/text, name the persona and task, compare against the chosen reference pattern, and state the exact fix.

batches.commitBoundary: Commit this remediation batch, refreshed evidence, judge outputs, scorecards, and tracker updates before the next UX feedback loop. If the committed pass still fails, the following pass starts by sending its tickets to the Remediation Planner.

plannerRules: Worker agents implement from remediation batches, not from optimistic summaries.
Product-spec work items must be completed and rerun before evidence repair or UI remediation work items for the same community are assigned.
Evidence repair work items must be completed and rerun before UI remediation work items for the same community/workflow/persona are assigned.
UI remediation work must be scoped by community/workflow/persona and target production surface, not by a broad global ticket summary.
The independent judge must rerun after each batch that changes UI, evidence, or critique.
No next UX feedback loop starts until the current remediation iteration is committed.
